newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bail set at $13.8 million for Banesto's Conde.
newsitem.headline: Bail set at $13.8 million for Banesto's Conde.

text.p: Former Banesto bank chairman Mario Conde was ordered on Wednesday to pay $13.8 million bail to remain free while appealing his conviction and six-year prison sentence in Spain's biggest financial scandal.
Spain's National High Court set the unusually high bail six days after Conde was found guilty of misappropriating 600 million pesetas in 1990 when he headed Banco Espanol de Credito-Banesto.
If Conde fails to pay the 2.0 billion pesetas ($13.8 million), he must start serving his sentence.
Conde, who together with close associates has been accused of massive fraud that led to the 1993 collapse of Banesto, was barred from leaving Spain and ordered to hand over his passport.
He will be tried later this year on further, related charges that carry even stiffer prison sentences.
The financier must also report twice weekly to the High Court and cannot change residences while awaiting Supreme Court ratification of his sentence.

In returning its verdict last week, the High Court ordered Conde to pay Banesto back the 600 million pesetas he allegedly funneled into Argentia Trust, a shadowy company based on the Lesser Antilles island of St. Vincent.
It was the first court decision arising so far from the Banesto case.
